rationale: Round 1 built and ran cleanly with no ICE, so this candidate shifts weight toward security and diversity while keeping cost sensitivity where this profile needs it: the binary is tiny (14161 text bytes, 39 functions), leaving ample size headroom, but the largest functions (_ZSt24__copy_move_backwa, _Z10deque_testPdS_i, the two _ZSt16__introsort_loop instantiations) are exactly the hot inner loops of sort/copy/container traversal, so RuntimeCost and SizeCost weights stay moderate-to-high for the expensive control-flow passes (BCF, FLA, IBR) to steer them away from those hot blocks rather than disabling them outright. FLA gets the highest SecurityGain/DiversityGain since flattening yields the strongest static-analysis resistance and the clean round-1 result suggests headroom to push it, tempered by a 0.45 CorrectnessRisk because this is template-heavy C++ where flattened loops and exception edges are the main correctness hazard. SUB and SPLIT are weighted aggressively (highest security/diversity, lowest cost/risk) because they are nearly free, compose well with flattening and branching passes, and arithmetic substitution lands well on this profile's arithmetic-heavy code (bignum Fibonacci in bigfib.cpp, Mandelbrot iteration in mandel-text.cpp). ICALL is favored on security over cost since indirection disrupts call-graph recovery across the many STL helper calls, while IGV is kept as a moderate all-rounder for global state used by the oopack/stepanov driver files.
